newsitem.title: USA: CBOT panel sees new contract lows coming for corn.
newsitem.headline: CBOT panel sees new contract lows coming for corn.

text.p: A Chicago Board of Trade-sponsored panel of analysts Tuesday said that the U.S. Agriculture Department's November forecast for a 9.265 billion bushel 1996 U.S. corn crop doesn't bode well for corn bulls.
"It looks like a pretty dismal picture for corn (prices). I believe new lows will be made," said Gregg Hunt a grain trader for Chicago-based trade house Rand Financial Services.
The contract low for March is $2.62-3/4 per bushel which was set November 5. March corn Monday ended at $2.71-3/4. Calls were for corn to open two to four cents lower Tuesday.
